items.name: diminished unison
items.typical_treatment: A diminished unison is a notational artefact rather than a sounding interval: it describes two voices on the same letter where the upper is lowered. It is retained here so spelling arithmetic stays total, and it carries a negative semitone size.

items.name: perfect unison
items.typical_treatment: Unison. Used for doubling and reinforcement; in independent counterpoint it collapses two voices into one and is normally reserved for arrivals.

items.name: augmented unison
items.typical_treatment: Augmented interval. Melodically awkward in strict profiles; harmonically it signals an altered or applied chord and resolves outward by step.

items.name: diminished second
items.typical_treatment: Diminished interval. Usually the inversion or contraction of an augmented interval; resolves inward by step and requires a spelling that reflects its destination.

items.name: minor second
items.typical_treatment: Dissonance. Prepare on a weak position and resolve by step in strict profiles; usable unprepared as chordal colour in jazz, neo-soul and ambient profiles.

items.name: perfect fourth
items.typical_treatment: Consonant between upper voices, dissonant when it is the interval above the bass. Prepare and resolve it against the bass in strict profiles; treat it as free colour in quartal and modal profiles.

items.name: augmented fourth
items.typical_treatment: Tritone. As the 3-to-7 frame of a dominant seventh it drives resolution outward to a sixth; as a melodic interval it is avoided in strict profiles.

items.name: diminished fifth
items.typical_treatment: Tritone spelled inward-resolving. Normally contracts to a third.

items.name: perfect fifth
items.typical_treatment: Perfect consonance. Approach by contrary or oblique motion in strict profiles; unrestricted in power-chord and planing profiles.
